Create a sparse counterfactual by zeroing contradicting variables

bl_find_sparse_cf.Rd

Builds a sparse version of the counterfactual that changes as few variables as needed. Starting from the observed point, it changes the variables whose Shapley contribution supports the prediction direction one at a time, largest absolute Shapley value first, and re-scores the model after each. It stops at the first point whose predicted class differs from the target's; the remaining variables stay at their observed values. Variables classified as "Contradicts", "No effect" or "Unknown", and any variable constrained as "fixed" in set_filters, are never changed. If no step crosses the boundary, every supporting variable has been changed and solution_valid is FALSE.

Usage

bl_find_sparse_cf(bl_shapley_result, round_to = NULL)

Arguments

bl_shapley_result

A "bl_shapley" object from bl_shapley.

round_to

Deprecated; must be NULL (the default). It rounded the changed values in model units without re-checking the constraints. Mark a whole-number feature "integer" in set_filters instead: bl_find_local_cf then rounds the counterfactual in raw units and re-checks it, and the sparse counterfactual takes its values from that counterfactual. See documentation/sparse-counterfactual.md section 3.

Value

A list of class "bl_sparse_result" with the following fields:

x_sparse

Single-row data frame; the sparse counterfactual in X-space.

pred_sparse

Scalar predicted probability of the sparse CF.

solution_valid

Logical; TRUE if the sparse CF flips the predicted class.

shapley_df

The annotated Shapley data frame with columns used_in_sparse (TRUE when the sparse CF changes the variable to its counterfactual value) and x_sparse_val.

sparse_path

Data frame, one row per step: step, variable (the variable changed), shapley (its Shapley value), pred (the model probability after the step) and crosses (whether the predicted class has flipped). Zero rows when no variable is a candidate.

bl_shapley

The "bl_shapley" object passed in.

Details

The selection follows the Shapley order, so it is not guaranteed to be the smallest possible subset: a smaller set outside that order may also cross.

Each changed variable takes its counterfactual value, so a feature marked "integer" in set_filters keeps the whole value that bl_find_local_cf rounded it to.
